Front: What is a lambda expression in Java?
Back: An anonymous implementation of the single abstract method of a functional interface. Example: `PaymentStrategy pix = payment -> PaymentStatus.APPROVED;`
An interface with exactly one abstract method. It may also have default methods, static methods and methods overriding Object's (equals, toString).

Front: Is @FunctionalInterface required? What does it do?
Back: No. Any single-abstract-method interface can be a lambda target. The annotation makes the compiler fail if a second abstract method is added, and documents intent.

Front: What is target typing for lambdas?
Back: A lambda has no type of its own; the compiler infers it from context. The same lambda text can be a PaymentStrategy or a Function<Payment, PaymentStatus>. `var x = p -> ...;` does not compile because there is no target.

Front: Why must local variables used inside a lambda be effectively final?
Back: The lambda captures a copy of the value, not the variable. Forbidding reassignment avoids confusing semantics and race conditions when the lambda runs later or on another thread. Fields are not restricted.

Front: What does `this` refer to inside a lambda vs an anonymous class?
Back: In a lambda, `this` is the enclosing instance (a lambda creates no new scope). In an anonymous class, `this` is the anonymous object itself.

Front: Can a lambda throw a checked exception?
Back: Only if the functional interface's method declares it. Otherwise catch it inside the lambda (often wrapping in an unchecked exception) or define an interface whose method declares `throws`.
A family of interchangeable behaviors behind one interface, with the concrete behavior chosen at runtime. The consumer depends only on the interface.

Front: How do you register a lambda as a Spring bean?
Back: Return it from a @Bean method in a @Configuration class. A lambda has no class to annotate with @Component. The bean type is the functional interface and the bean name defaults to the method name.

Front: What happens if two beans of the same type exist and you inject one by type?
Back: Startup fails with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException. Fix with @Qualifier("beanName"), @Primary, or by injecting List<T> / Map<String,T>.

Front: What does Spring inject for `Map<String, PaymentStrategy>`?
Back: Every bean of type PaymentStrategy, keyed by bean name (e.g. "pixStrategy" → PIX lambda). String keys are fragile: a typo only fails at runtime.

Front: switch expression vs strategy map for choosing a strategy?
Back: switch over an enum is exhaustive and checked at compile time, but adding a method means editing the service. A Map<PaymentMethod, PaymentStrategy> lets you add behavior in config only, but a missing entry is detected at runtime.

Front: When should a strategy be a class instead of a lambda bean?
Back: When it has its own dependencies (gateway, repository, logger), non-trivial logic, or needs its own unit tests. Lambdas suit very short, stateless behavior.
